topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture by linking prior histopathology practicals to the day's learning outcomes regarding cellular transformation, cancer genetics, and genetic instability.

topics.label: Tumor Virology and Experimental Assays of Cellular Transformation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of transforming viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and established laboratory assays to measure cell transformation.

topics.label: Classification and Genetic Mechanics of Oncogenes and Tumor Suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the major classes of cancer-associated genes and explain how mutations disrupt cell cycle control and protein function through dominant, recessive, and dominant-negative mechanisms.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Genetic Instability and Multi-Step Tumor Progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how failures in DNA repair, replication, and chromosome segregation generate genetic instability to accelerate the stepwise accumulation of mutations in tumor progression.

topics.label: Hereditary Cancer Predisposition and Tumor Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how inherited germline mutations accelerate cancer onset and shape ongoing tumor evolution and therapy response.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Recommended Reading
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with closing housekeeping, an invitation for questions, recommended reading, and a look ahead to the next session.
